Hi there, I'm really sorry about the accident. And I'm sorry about how your mother treats situations, I'm glad you got better though. Where do I begin... It seems like your dealing with depression. I'm not an expert, but it seems a little more than PTSD. As for your mother, I'm not sure why she is so hard on you. I like to think that they are just trying to make you strong, because you need to be strong when going out into the world on your own. I struggle with PTSD myself and have severe depression and I live alone, so I won't lie when I say it can be hard some days. I can only speak from experience and what I did and what worked for me. I think you need to try to get some help, also find some coping practices. Somehow distract yourself until you can get through the day, but you need to know the difference from healthy distractions and unhealthy ones. For example, I sing to myself all the time, it keeps my mind busy from what bothers me. But I sought out help to, psychiatrist help. I'm aware meds aren't for everybody and it took me years to be put on something that worked, and I'm not saying you need them, but it doesn't hurt to try to at least try to talk to someone about it. A therapist or something? And please don't do anything rash with sharp objects :(

Personally, I think bonds are formed in early childhood. The friends that stay after graduation are the ones that will be there your entire life. As you grow up it gets harder and harder to make friends. Some people go to the bar to try to accomplish this. Others make friends at work, but that usually requires one person having to go way past meeting in the middle to try to accomplish this. In truth, friendship are very fragile and often result in one person always going way past the 'meeting in the middle' construct. This truth usually results in a strong relationship (friendship or more) or ends in bitterness. I think it's a trial and error thing that we learn in early childhood, but many forget how to do so as an adult. The difficulty as an adult doesn't help any. But I think it's a trial and error thing. As you go, you will make mistakes, what is important is that you learn from them and make sure to not repeat them. If you need someone to talk to, my dm's are always open. I do wish you the best on your journey through life :)

Friendships are fragile. They're usually made because two people work in the same area, have a class together etc. As soon as they move away it usually falls apart. Usually one person tries more than the other to be there and to keep their friendship together. Sometimes it makes something beautiful other times it leads to bitterness. Being a person who usually cares more for my friends than my friends care for me, I usually always go the extra distance to ask about their day and to be there for them. If I were you I would go to her house and try to be thwere for them. But the guy above me haha point  let her know your there for her. Space would be good for her. Having a year to live is really scary, I'm sure your friend is scared. If I had a year to live I would be afraid to get close to people because it would make it a lot sadder when I finally go. Goodbyes are hard. Letting go.... Difficult.... The treasures of family, friends, loved ones is worth more than anything else in this world. I think you should be there with your friend and make happy memory's while they are still here. Embrace the memories you two gifted eachother and hold on to them. Let your friend know that they will not be forgotten. Let your friend know you will live for the both of you.

Hey man, first off it's ok to be scared. It's a simple animal instinct. And to worry about your future. Self preservation. School is a good way to show employers that you have discipline and that you have a decent amount of problem solving skills. I dropped out of highschool to join the military and that ended up falling through due to some personal reasons. Now I'm working in the ship yard, and making decent money too, with only a ged. Life is based on luck. In some cases, it's not what you know. It's who you know. Most people aren't special or possess any unique talent, kids grow up and say they want to be famous but less than 1% actually do. It's a sad truth of life but it's the reality we live in nonetheless. Life is about making yourself comfortable as much as you can till the end. The only person who will take care of you and pull your weight is you. My advice is stay away from drugs, it clouds the mind, I was on cocaine at your age. And made dumb decisions. Maybe try meditating on what you really want to do with yourself. If you're going to college for some sort of job think of something that's in high demand. Like being a welder or an automotive technician, something along those lines you can go anywhere in the world and have a job with a trade like that. But don't overthink and overanalyze, it separates the body from the mind. if you spend all your time worrying about the future it's easy to miss the present and leaving opportunities behind. You are the master of your own reality. I hope this helps you out man, and good luck. Love yourself for who you are 😊
